from: chapitre 3 de la vidéo longue (la course des procédés ; coupé : la mise en garde sur les noms de procédés, le retard du 7 nm d'Intel et la chute de l'action ; phrases resserrées)
paragraphs: In 2013, Intel said its {ten-nanometer|10 nm} chips could reach the market by 2015.
That slipped to 2016. Then to the second half of 2017. Real volume only came in 2019.
Meanwhile, TSMC started volume production of its {seven-nanometer|7 nm} process in 2018, and {five nanometers|5 nm} in 2020. The most advanced factories in the world weren't Intel's anymore.
In June 2020, Apple announced it would drop Intel processors from its Macs, for chips of its own design, built by TSMC.

AMD, with no factories of its own since 2009, rode TSMC's lead too. In 2017, it had less than {one percent|1%} of server processors. By early 2026, it earned {forty-six percent|46%} of all the money spent on x86 server processors.
Intel's great advantage, making its own chips, had become its biggest weakness. Full story on the channel.
